documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 32F.

Interval: Feeling well. No palpitations or heat intolerance since the fall episode cleared. Weight back near her usual. Still teaching classes 3x/week. Endo plans to see her in the fall.

Meds: levothyroxine 112 mcg daily (endo), calcium carbonate 600 mg / D3 400 IU BID.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: never smoker, rare alcohol. Same job.
PHQ-9: 1.

Exam: Vitals per flowsheet. Well appearing. HEENT unremarkable. Neck: healed incision, no masses, no lymphadenopathy. Heart regular rate and rhythm, no murmur. Lungs clear. Breasts without masses, axillae negative. Abdomen soft, nontender. Pelvic: external genitalia normal, cervix without lesions, Pap/HPV collected. Extremities without edema. Skin no rash. No tremor.

A/P:
1. Preventive: Pap with HPV co-test today (last Pap 2022). CBC, CMP. Flu and COVID this fall.
2. Postsurgical hypothyroidism / hx papillary thyroid ca: TSH and free T4 today, copy to endo. Thyrotoxicosis from the fall has not recurred.
3. Calcium supplement: calcium on CMP.

RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Results from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Lisa, your blood work from the physical all looks good. Thyroid numbers are in range, calcium is normal, blood counts normal. The Pap and HPV results usually take about a week; I'll send a note when they're in.

documents.title: Pap result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Pap and HPV are both negative. With a normal co-test you won't need another for five years.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology, regional endocrine group
Date of visit: 10/07/2025

Dear Doctor,

Ms. Callahan returned for her yearly follow-up of papillary thyroid carcinoma, treated by total thyroidectomy with central neck dissection in 2019, and her postsurgical hypothyroidism.

She feels well. The palpitations, sweating and weight loss of last fall resolved within weeks and have not returned. She takes levothyroxine 112 mcg each morning and her calcium with vitamin D twice daily. No drug allergies.

Exam: vitals as recorded. Comfortable. Thyroid bed and lateral neck without mass or palpable lymph nodes. No tremor.

Labs today: TSH and free T4 within the reference range; thyroglobulin <0.1 ng/mL, undetectable.

Assessment: no clinical or biochemical evidence of disease. Replacement is adequate.

Plan: levothyroxine 112 mcg unchanged. Calcium/vitamin D unchanged. Return in one year with TSH, free T4 and thyroglobulin beforehand.

Allergies: NKDA

Sincerely,
Endocrinology

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (2025-26) left deltoid IM, COVID (2025-26 formula) right deltoid IM. No contraindications on screening. Tolerated well, observed 15 min. Last year she had a sore arm for a day, nothing else.

TECHNIQUE: Oral I-123 capsule given 03/30/2026 at 10:30. Neck counts with thyroid probe at 24 hours, background corrected.

documents.title: Endocrinology Visit Letter
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology, regional endocrine group
Date of visit: 03/30/2026

Dear Doctor,

I saw Ms. Callahan on 03/30. Her roommate came with her and, with her permission, stayed for the visit.

She came in with anxiety, heavy sweating and swings in mood, which she says feel much like October 2024. Her roommate has noticed that she has become very focused on fitness lately and has been on strict diets and hard exercise routines. She has lost 8 lb in two months while her appetite has been good. When I asked about supplements she told me she has been buying 'metabolism boosters' online. She takes no prescription medicine apart from her levothyroxine.

Current medicines: levothyroxine 112 mcg daily; calcium carbonate 600 mg / vitamin D3 400 IU twice daily; the online products. No drug allergies. Family history negative for thyroid disease.

Exam: pulse 102, BP 130/80. Alert and cooperative, visibly jittery. The thyroid bed is non-palpable, with no nodularity or tenderness.

We did labs and a radioiodine uptake. TSH <0.01, free T4 2.8 ng/dL, free T3 6.6 pg/mL, thyroglobulin <0.1 ng/mL. 24-hour uptake 0.5%.

Impression: recurrent thyrotoxicosis factitia. Undetectable thyroglobulin and negligible uptake again point to hormone from outside, and the online products are the likely source; products sold this way frequently contain thyroid hormone or thyroid extract.

Plan:
- Stop all of the online products now. She agreed.
- Levothyroxine 112 mcg unchanged.
- TSH and free T4 in 6 weeks, at your office as before.
- Her roommate's concern about her eating and exercise seemed worth passing on. I would be grateful if you could see her soon and follow up on it.
- Yearly surveillance visit in the fall as planned.

Allergies: NKDA

Sincerely,
Endocrinology

documents.title: Saw endo Monday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I saw my endocrinologist Monday and my thyroid was too high again. She thinks it was the supplements I was taking, so I threw them out. She said I should check in with you too. Can I get an appointment in the next couple weeks? Mornings are best.

documents.title: RE: Saw endo Monday
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Lisa, you're booked Tuesday 4/14 at 8:40 with the doctor. We got the letter from endocrinology yesterday. See you then.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u after endo 3/30. Letter reviewed: recurrent exogenous thyrotoxicosis (TSH <0.01, FT4 2.8, Tg undetectable, low uptake), felt due to online 'metabolism booster' products. Endo asked us to follow up on the eating/exercise concern her roommate raised.

S: Stopped the products 3/31 and threw them out. Sweats and jitteriness easing, sleeping better. Over the winter she cut back a lot on what she was eating and added extra workouts on top of her classes. Agrees that was too much. No CP, no syncope.

O: Vitals per flowsheet, HR and BP normal today. Wt 70.4 kg. Calm, engaged. No tremor. Neck no mass. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear.

A/P:
1. Thyrotoxicosis factitia, recurrent: off the products. Recheck TSH/FT4 around 5/11 per endo. Levothyroxine 112 unchanged.
2. Eating and exercise: talked through regular meals around her teaching schedule and keeping to her usual class load for now. She was open to it. Asked her to bring any supplement to us or endo before taking it. Will check in at labs and at her physical in June.

~30 min, majority counseling.

documents.title: Thyroid recheck
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: TSH and free T4 normal again, six weeks off the supplements. Sent to endo. Messaged Lisa: good news, stay on the 112 mcg, nothing else. Resolving thyrotoxicosis on the problem list.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, 34F.

Interval: Recurrent exogenous thyrotoxicosis this spring from online supplements; off them since 3/31 and TSH/FT4 normal 5/11. Says she feels back to herself. Eating regular meals, teaching her usual three classes, dropped the extra sessions. No supplements. Weight 72.6, up from 70.4 in April.

Meds: levothyroxine 112 mcg daily (endo), calcium carbonate 600 mg / D3 400 IU BID.
Allergies: NKDA.
PHQ-9: 2.

Exam: Vitals per flowsheet. Well. HEENT normal. Neck: healed scar, no mass, no nodes. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. Ext no edema. Skin normal. No tremor.

A/P:
1. Preventive: Pap/HPV 2025 negative, next 2030. Lipids 2024 fine. CBC, CMP today. Flu/COVID in the fall.
2. Hypothyroidism / hx papillary thyroid ca: TSH/FT4 today, endo visit in the fall.
3. Eating/exercise: doing well by her account and by weight. Keep checking in.

RTC October for flu shot and a quick check.

documents.title: Your labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lisa, labs from Wednesday are all normal, including the thyroid tests. Nice work this spring. See you in October.
